rules.note: a channel-hopping jammer produces a spread of hot/cold channels in the scan (direct emitter evidence) plus recurring long fade runs as it revisits each channel periodically
a wideband jammer raises the noise floor uniformly, so the scan finds essentially every channel bad with low spread between channels
a single-channel jammer taints only some channels, leaving clean alternates, so the scan shows a large spread between good and bad channels with no periodic fade pattern
a reactive jammer only keys on our transmissions, so loss is concentrated as shadow-loss on our own tx attempts yet decoupled from the normal RSSI-PDR relationship, unlike pure link-quality effects
self-inflicted collision loss tracks RSSI closely (weak links fail more under load) and yields essentially zero silent/undecodable loss since packets are lost to collision, not to a hidden emitter
a physically lost node stops sending heartbeats entirely (large positive heartbeat gap) while surviving links still show ordinary RSSI-correlated behavior
